name: Eyelid glue
summary: Cosmetic adhesive that sticks the lid skin into a temporary crease; little published research exists on the product itself.
lead: Eyelid glue is a cosmetic adhesive applied to the upper eyelid to hold the skin in a fold, giving the appearance of a double eyelid for a limited time. It is a non-surgical alternative to double eyelid surgery, which creates a permanent crease .

name: Canthal tilt tape (lateral eye lift tape)
summary: Tape pulled toward the temple to angle the outer eye corners upward; no studies were found.
lead: Canthal tilt tape, also called lateral eye lift tape, is a temporary cosmetic aid in which tape is attached near the outer eye corner and pulled toward the temple to alter the apparent angle of the eye. The canthi are the corners of the eye where the upper and lower lids meet; the lateral canthus is the outer corner and the medial canthus the inner corner .

name: Winged eyeliner for tilt
summary: Extending liner outward and upward to suggest a more tilted outer eye corner; a makeup technique with no studies on its effect on perceived tilt.
lead: Winged eyeliner defines the upper lid and extends the line outward to a point about halfway toward the end of the eyebrow. A related style, cat eye, uses a thicker wing that runs along both upper and lower lash lines .

name: Tightlining / waterline liner
summary: Liner applied at the lash roots or waterline to darken the lash line; no studies on its effect on perceived eye depth.
lead: Tightlining is a method of eyeliner application in which liner is placed close to the waterline, under the upper lashes and above the lower lashes. Waterproof products are usually preferred, and the technique can make lashes appear longer .

name: Guyliner / kohl
summary: Eyeliner worn by men, from ancient kohl to 2000s emo guyliner; discussed for an intense look, with documented lead concerns about some traditional kohl.
lead: Kohl is a soft, usually black powder used around the eyes. Traditional kohl was made by grinding stibnite (antimony sulfide), and many modern and homemade versions use galena (lead sulfide); Western manufacturers generally use carbon or charcoal . Egyptians of all social classes are reported to have worn it from about 3100 BCE, and both men and women appear in tomb depictions .

name: Eyelash growth serum (peptide, OTC)
summary: Drug-free cosmetic serums for lash length; popular in forums, but no published trials of the peptide versions.
lead: Over-the-counter eyelash growth serums are cosmetic liquids or gels applied along the lash line with the aim of making eyelashes look longer, thicker or fuller. Many are marketed as drug-free alternatives to prescription prostaglandin products, and typically list peptides, conditioning agents, botanical extracts or vitamins as their active ingredients rather than a prostaglandin analogue.
claims: Lash serums can make lashes visibly thicker
Minoxidil can be combined with or substituted for lash serum
Oils such as castor or rosemary oil work like serums

name: Lash extensions
summary: Salon-applied individual lashes bonded to your own for length and fullness, lasting a few weeks per set.
lead: Lash extensions are individual synthetic (or sometimes natural-material) lashes attached by a technician to a person's own lashes with semi-permanent adhesive, to add length, curl and fullness. According to Wikipedia, an application typically takes up to two hours and lasts about three to four weeks depending on care.

name: Lash tint
summary: Salon dye to darken lashes; regulators in the US say no dyes are approved for the eye area.
lead: Lash tinting is a salon procedure in which a dye is applied to eyelashes to darken them, so they look fuller without mascara. Wikipedia lists tints, alongside extensions, among popular salon eyelash procedures.

name: Eyebrow growth serum
summary: Peptide and botanical brow serums are popular online; published evidence centres on prescription bimatoprost, not the OTC products.
lead: Eyebrow growth serums are topical cosmetic products, often containing peptides or botanical extracts, marketed to make sparse brows look denser or fuller. They are discussed in looksmaxxing communities alongside castor oil, microneedling, minoxidil and prescription prostaglandin analogues.
claims: Specific peptides can stimulate brow hair growth
Microneedling helps brow growth
Castor oil regrows brows
Prostaglandin analogues thicken brows

name: Castor oil on brows/lashes
summary: Folk remedy of brushing castor oil on brows and lashes for thickness; popular online, untested in trials.
lead: Applying castor oil to eyebrows and eyelashes is a folk remedy that practitioners say thickens or lengthens them. Castor oil is pressed from castor beans and consists mostly of triglycerides, with ricinoleic acid making up most of its fatty acids.
claims: Castor oil regrows shaved or thinned brows

name: Eyebrow microblading
summary: Semi-permanent pigment strokes tattooed into the brows; popular for fuller brows, with case reports of infection and allergy.
lead: Microblading is a semi-permanent cosmetic tattooing technique in which a technician uses a handheld tool with fine blades or needles to draw hair-like strokes of pigment into the upper dermis of the eyebrows. It is used to fill sparse, thin or uneven brows and to disguise brow loss.
claims: Microblading gives men thicker, darker brows that improve attractiveness
Results look unnatural on men
Minoxidil, dermastamping and castor oil are alternatives
Microblading carries infection and allergy risks

name: Powder / ombre / nano brows
summary: Machine-applied semi-permanent brow tattoo for a soft shaded fill; popular salon service with no dedicated studies.
lead: Powder, ombre and nano brows are names used for semi-permanent cosmetic eyebrow tattooing in which pigment is deposited with a machine rather than drawn stroke by stroke by hand. Powder and ombre styles aim for a soft, shaded, make-up-like fill that is typically lighter at the front of the brow and darker toward the tail, while nano brows use very fine needles for a subtler result. These terms are trade and salon vocabulary rather than medical ones.

name: Henna brows
summary: Plant-dye stain on brow hair and skin that lasts days to weeks; the main documented hazard is adulterated 'black henna'.
lead: Henna brows are a salon service in which a paste made from henna, a plant dye, is applied to the eyebrow hairs and underlying skin to darken or define them. The staining agent in henna is lawsone, which is released when the dried leaves are powdered and made into a paste . Because the stain sits on the skin surface and hair, it is temporary.

name: Brow shaving / brow reshaping for tilt
summary: Trimming or reshaping the brows to change how tilted the eye area looks; cheap and reversible, with no studies on its effect on perceived tilt.
lead: Brow reshaping for tilt refers to trimming, shaving or otherwise altering the eyebrows to change how the eye area appears angled, a concern in looksmaxxing discussions of positive canthal tilt and the 'hunter eyes' look. In everyday grooming this is done by removing or trimming hair; Wikipedia lists tweezing, waxing, threading and trimming as common methods, and notes that some people shave the brows and draw them on .

name: Brow thread lift
summary: Threads placed to hoist the brow tail without surgery; evidence is thin, with one trial on durability just registered.
lead: A brow thread lift is a minimally invasive procedure in which threads are placed under the skin to suspend and raise the tail of the eyebrow. It is offered as an alternative to surgical brow lifts, which Wikipedia describes as procedures to raise drooping brows, with types including endoscopic, coronal and direct approaches, and non-surgical options such as botulinum toxin .

name: Orbital rim implants
summary: Silicone or porous implants set along the lower orbital rim for under-eye bony support; popular in hardmaxxing talk, thin on published data.
lead: Infraorbital or orbital rim implants are alloplastic (synthetic) devices placed along the lower orbital rim to add bony support under the eye. Grokipedia describes them as typically made of medical-grade silicone, intended for tear trough hollows, rim recession and a negative orbital vector, and presented as a more durable alternative to fillers or fat grafting .
claims: Off-the-shelf malar implants look feminine, so men need custom implants
Rim implants can change the cheek contour (ogee curve) and appearance of facial fullness

name: Infraorbital rim / zygomatic filler
summary: Hyaluronic acid filler placed around the under-eye rim and cheekbone for support; temporary, with a delicate and risky injection area.
lead: Infraorbital rim and zygomatic filler refers to injectable fillers, usually hyaluronic acid, placed around the lower orbital rim and cheekbone to add apparent support under the eye. Wikipedia describes injectable fillers as materials used to smooth wrinkles, restore volume and contour areas such as the cheeks . In appearance communities the aim is often described as building skeletal-looking support for a deeper-set, more supported eye region.

name: Fat grafting (lower eyelid / tear trough)
summary: Moving your own fat into the under-eye hollow to soften the tear trough: a real surgical option backed mostly by case series, with lumps and irregularities among the reported complications.
lead: Fat grafting of the lower eyelid and tear trough, also called periorbital lipofilling or autologous fat transfer, is a surgical procedure in which a patient's own fat is harvested from another part of the body, processed and injected into the hollow beneath the lower eyelid to restore volume and smooth the transition to the cheek .
claims: Fat grafting can fix hollow eyelids and make the eye area look better.
Fat grafting may only treat symptoms if there is an underlying ptosis problem.

name: Transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty
summary: Lower-eyelid surgery through an incision inside the lid, so there is no outer scar, used to remove or reposition under-eye fat bags.
lead: Transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty is a form of lower-eyelid surgery in which the incision is made on the inner surface of the eyelid, leaving no external scar . It is used to remove or reposition the orbital fat that produces under-eye bags and tear trough hollowing.

name: Plasma pen blepharoplasty
summary: A handheld plasma device used on eyelid skin to tighten it without surgery; popular in DIY and salon circles, with almost no published clinical research behind it.
lead: Plasma pen blepharoplasty, also called plasma fibroblasting eyelid lift, is a non-surgical cosmetic procedure that uses a handheld plasma device to tighten loose or wrinkled eyelid skin. It is promoted as an alternative to surgical blepharoplasty.
claims: A plasma pen can tighten eyelid skin and give a better eye area without surgery.
Cheap home devices give results comparable to clinic treatments.

name: Polynucleotide eye filler
summary: Polynucleotide injections around the eyes for thin, crepey lower-lid skin; very little published evidence turned up for the periorbital use.
lead: Polynucleotide eye filler is a name for injections of polynucleotide-based products into the thin skin of the lower eyelid and surrounding area, intended to improve the quality of periorbital skin.

name: Eyelid RF/laser tightening
summary: Fractional lasers (and radiofrequency devices) used to tighten loose eyelid skin without surgery; small studies show modest improvement, while heavy laxity is usually treated surgically.
lead: Eyelid RF/laser tightening refers to non-surgical treatments that use laser or radiofrequency energy to firm lax eyelid skin and reduce fine lines, as an alternative to surgical blepharoplasty.

name: Vitamin K eye cream
summary: Topical vitamin K marketed for under-eye dark circles said to have a blood-vessel component; the sources reviewed contain no clinical studies of it.
lead: Vitamin K eye cream is a topical cosmetic product containing vitamin K, applied under the eyes and marketed for dark circles that are thought to have a vascular component, meaning visible blood vessels or pooled blood beneath thin skin.

name: Dermal rollers / microneedling eyes
summary: Needling the thin skin around the eyes, claimed to thicken it and soften circles; microneedling has some evidence for scars, little specific to eyes.
lead: Microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy, skin needling or dermarolling, is a cosmetic procedure that repeatedly punctures the skin with tiny sterile needles. Handheld rollers and stamping devices are used by clinicians, and rollers are also sold for home use.

name: Bates method eye exercises
summary: Early-20th-century relaxation and eye-movement routines promoted to improve vision; reviews find no objective gain in eyesight.
lead: The Bates method is a system of eye relaxation and eye-movement exercises developed by the American eye physician William Horatio Bates (1860-1931) and promoted as a way to improve eyesight without corrective lenses. Bates published his main statement of the method in 1920 in a book titled The Cure of Imperfect Sight by Treatment Without Glasses, also issued as Perfect Sight Without Glasses.
claims: Eye relaxation exercises like palming can improve eyesight and reduce myopia without glasses.
Glasses weaken the eyes and cause dependency.
Sunning (exposing the eyes to sunlight) strengthens the eyes.
The eyeball changes shape through the external eye muscles to focus, rather than the lens.

name: Hair bangs / frame hairstyle for eyes
summary: Fringe and face-framing hair used to draw attention to the eyes and brow area; a styling choice with little formal research behind the claims.
lead: Bangs, called fringe in British, Australian and New Zealand English, are strands of hair that fall over the front hairline to cover the forehead, usually just above the eyebrows. Their length and shape vary, and modern Western cuts are usually straight, though arc-shaped and ragged versions exist.

name: Eye whitening and brightening
summary: Efforts to make the whites of the eyes look whiter and brighter, discussed for contrast and a fresher look; little research targets this goal.
lead: Eye whitening and brightening is a looksmaxxing topic concerned with how white and clear the sclera looks and how bright the eyes appear. On looksmax.org, one user argued that sclera whiteness and brightness matter for every eye colour because of contrast, and said it is especially important for brown eyes; he asked others for ways to whiten the sclera and mentioned eye drops.
claims: White sclera and bright eyes improve eye appearance through contrast.
Eye drops can be used to whiten the sclera.

name: Non-surgical rhinoplasty (liquid nose job)
summary: Injectable filler used to smooth a bump, lift the tip or add projection without surgery; results are temporary and rare vascular complications can be severe.
lead: Non-surgical rhinoplasty, also called liquid rhinoplasty, is a cosmetic procedure that reshapes the nose with injectable filler instead of surgery. Wikipedia describes it as using fillers such as collagen or hyaluronic acid to fill depressed areas, lift the angle of the tip or smooth bumps on the bridge, without changing the size of the nose.

name: Septoplasty
summary: Functional surgery that straightens a deviated nasal septum to improve breathing; it is not a cosmetic nose reshaping, though the two are often combined.
lead: Septoplasty is a surgical procedure that straightens a deviated nasal septum, the partition between the two nasal cavities, to relieve obstruction. It is also called septal reconstruction or submucous septal resection. It is performed through the nostrils, under local or general anaesthesia, and most operations take about an hour or less according to Wikipedia.
claims: A functional septoplasty can be used to make small cosmetic changes to the nose, such as the tip.
Septoplasty alone may not straighten a crooked-looking nose, so some wait for or combine rhinoplasty or jaw surgery.
Turbinate reduction risks empty nose syndrome.

name: Septorhinoplasty
summary: Combined surgery on the nasal septum and the outer nose, done for breathing and shape together; the evidence base is mostly surgical case series, with recovery details well documented.
lead: Septorhinoplasty is an operation that combines septoplasty, which corrects a deviated nasal septum, with rhinoplasty, which reshapes the external nose. It is used when a patient has both an obstructed airway and an aesthetic concern, for example a crooked nose following trauma. Surgeons describe it as a common functional-aesthetic procedure, and trials registered in several countries study its recovery, pain control and outcomes.
claims: A crooked nose with a slightly deviated septum calls for septorhinoplasty rather than rhinoplasty alone.
Braces or aligners should be timed relative to nose surgery because they could put pressure on the nose.
A very upturned tip right after surgery is normal and drops over time.
Telling the surgeon repeatedly not to make the nose upturned gives a natural, straight result.
